You hit on one of the most interesting aspects of relativity. The person in the ship traveling at relativistic speeds wouldn't grow younger, but time for them relative to the people back on earth would slow down. This phenomena is called The Twin Paradox which you can find a million hits for if you google it I'm sure. So yes let's say I travel a million light years away, turn around and travel a million light years back. And I was traveling at such a velocity that from my perspective it only took 20 years. From the perspective of somebody back on earth 2 million years will have passed. Suffice to say Earth would look pretty different when you returned.

We actually can measure this! The typical example is the GPS satellites rotating around our planet. Due to relativistic effects the atomic clocks on board these satellites tick at a different rate than they do on earth. In fact the precision required by these satellites is such that if we don't mathematically account for the relativistic effects on the clocks, the errors in GPS readings would accumulate at the rate of about 10km a day!

Another example is Mercury. Mercury is small enough and close enough to the sun that there are visibly detectable relativistic effects. In fact we measured them about a century before relativity was discovered. Since at the time we were relying on Newtonian physics for everything we assumed there was some tiny planet between Mercury and the sun (we named it Vulcan) that was causing the orbital perturbations of the planet. Astronomers worldwide desperately sought out the planet for more than a century! The perturbations match up perfectly with what is expected by relativity.

And finally we've constantly tested relativity with various probes to incredibly high degrees of accuracy. It always comes out perfectly. It's so bizarre and amazing that I almost feel like I'm describing a sci fi plot when I talk about more than a realistic depiction of how our universe actually functions. It also makes you wonder what other wonders of the universe are out there waiting to be discovered.
